# AC Plus Heating & Air

> AC Plus Heating & Air is an air conditioning and heating contractor serving the High Desert and Inland Empire regions of Southern California from four locations, offering air conditioning installation, repair, replacement, maintenance, and 24-hour emergency service.

Location: Victorville, CA  
Phone: (760) 474-5776  
Website: https://acplushvac.com  
Knowledge base: https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site

## Knowledge base articles

- [Split System AC Installation](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/split-system-ac-installation): Split system AC installation, or mini-split installation, is a type of air conditioning installation that mounts a separate indoor air handler and outdoor condenser unit, connects them with refrigerant lines, and wires the system to a dedicated 240V circuit so a building can be cooled without ductwork.
- [Ductless Mini-Split Air Conditioner](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/ductless-mini-split-air-conditioner): A ductless mini-split air conditioner conditions one or more rooms without ductwork.
- [Multi-Zone Mini-Split Installation](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/multi-zone-mini-split-installation): Multi-Zone Mini-Split Installation, called zoned ductless AC installation, is a type of air conditioning installation that connects one outdoor condenser unit to multiple indoor air handlers, each cooling or heating a separate room or zone independently, without ductwork, without shared airflow, and without the temperature compromises that come from a single thermostat controlling an entire building.
- [Packaged AC Unit Installation](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/packaged-ac-unit-installation): Packaged AC unit installation, called rooftop AC installation, is a type of Air Conditioning Installation in which all system components.
- [New Construction Air Conditioning Installation](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/new-construction-air-conditioning-installation): New construction air conditioning installation.
- [AC System Replacement](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/ac-system-replacement): AC System Replacement, called an Air Conditioner System Changeout, is the full removal of an existing cooling system and the installation of a new one, covering the outdoor condenser unit, the indoor air handler or evaporator coil, refrigerant lines, and the electrical connections that tie everything together.
- [AC Unit Upgrade Installation](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/ac-unit-upgrade-installation): AC Unit Upgrade Installation, called AC System Replacement, is a full-scope HVAC service that removes an existing air conditioner and installs a new, higher-capacity or higher-efficiency unit in its place, covering equipment removal and disposal, new condenser mounting, refrigerant line connection, electrical disconnect work, ductwork integration and thermostat configuration.
- [Air Conditioning System Sizing](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/air-conditioning-system-sizing): Air Conditioning System Sizing.
- [Evaporator Coil](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/evaporator-coil): An evaporator coil, called an A-coil or cooling coil, is a heat exchanger installed inside an air conditioning system.
- [Condensate Drain System](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/condensate-drain-system): A condensate drain system.
- [Condensate Drain Line](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/condensate-drain-line): A condensate drain line.
- [Concrete Equipment Pad](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/concrete-equipment-pad): A concrete equipment pad.
- [Electrical Disconnect Switch](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/electrical-disconnect-switch): An electrical disconnect switch, called an AC disconnect box, is a type of electrical safety equipment that manually cuts off all power to an air conditioning unit.
- [R-32 Refrigerant](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/r-32-refrigerant): R-32 Refrigerant, known as HFC-32 or difluoromethane, is a single-component hydrofluorocarbon refrigerant with the chemical formula CH2F2, a molecular weight of 52.02 g/mol, a boiling point of -51.7°C at standard atmospheric pressure, a Global Warming Potential of 675, and a flammability classification of A2L, making it one of the more widely adopted modern refrigerants in residential and commercial air conditioning systems across the United States and globally.
- [HVAC Ductwork](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/hvac-ductwork): HVAC ductwork, called ducting, is a network of air distribution channels that carries conditioned air from a heating or cooling unit to every room in a building, including supply ducts that push treated air out, return ducts that pull stale air back, plenums, fittings, and vents.
- [Ductwork Installation](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/ductwork-installation): Ductwork installation, called ducting installation, is the fabrication and fitting of an air distribution system within a building structure.
- [Air Distribution System](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/air-distribution-system): An air distribution system, or duct system, is a network of ducts, vents, registers, dampers and plenums that moves conditioned air from a central heating or cooling unit to every room in a building and returns stale air back to the unit for reconditioning.
- [Air Vents](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/air-vents): Air vents, called air registers or diffusers, are openings fitted with grilles, louvers, damper blades and mounting frames that allow conditioned air to enter a room, control the direction of airflow and regulate how much air each space receives.
- [HVAC Zoning System](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/hvac-zoning-system): An HVAC zoning system, called a zoned HVAC system, divides a building into independent temperature-controlled areas.
- [Equipment Placement](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/equipment-placement): Equipment Placement, called Unit Siting, is the deliberate process of positioning AC units at specified locations within a structure, covering indoor unit height, outdoor condenser clearance, mount surface load-bearing capacity, orientation relative to sun and airflow, and the distance from walls, obstructions and heat sources.
- [Insulation](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/insulation): Insulation, called thermal insulation, is a building material designed to slow heat transfer between spaces.
- [Inadequate Cooling Capacity](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/inadequate-cooling-capacity): Inadequate cooling capacity, called poor cooling performance, is a condition where an air conditioning unit's BTU output falls short of the space's actual cooling load, leaving rooms warmer than the thermostat setpoint regardless of how long the system runs.
- [Inefficient Cooling](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/inefficient-cooling): Inefficient cooling, called low cooling efficiency, is a measurable condition in which an air conditioning system fails to deliver its rated cooling output at expected energy consumption levels, producing symptoms that include a temperature differential greater than 2°F from the thermostat setpoint, a SEER value below the unit's rated figure, elevated kWh draw, slower-than-normal time to reach the desired temperature and a BTU/hr output that falls short of the system's nameplate capacity.
- [Uneven Indoor Temperatures](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/uneven-indoor-temperatures): Uneven indoor temperatures, called HVAC imbalance, are an Indoor Air Comfort Problem defined by inconsistent air temperature distribution across different rooms or zones within a building.
- [High Utility Bills](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/high-utility-bills): High utility bills represent a measurable Energy Cost Problem.
- [High Energy Bills](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/high-energy-bills): High energy bills, or elevated utility costs, are a measurable financial problem caused by excessive electrical consumption from HVAC equipment, particularly air conditioning systems running in hot climates like the Mojave Desert, where cooling loads push monthly consumption well above baseline for weeks at a time.
- [End-of-Life HVAC System](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/end-of-life-hvac-system): An end-of-life HVAC system has exceeded its functional service lifespan.
- [Obsolete AC System](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/obsolete-ac-system): An obsolete AC system is an air conditioning system that no longer meets current efficiency, refrigerant, or building code standards.
- [Failed Compressor](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/failed-compressor): A failed compressor, called compressor burnout, is a type of AC component failure in which the compressor can no longer pressurize refrigerant through the cooling cycle, causing the entire air conditioning system to stop producing cold air.
- [R-22 Phase-Out](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/r-22-phase-out): The R-22 Phase-Out, formally known as the HCFC-22 Regulatory Ban, is a U.S.
- [Duct Sealing](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/duct-sealing): Duct sealing, called HVAC Duct Sealing, is a type of HVAC System Efficiency Service that closes gaps, cracks and disconnected joints in a home's ductwork to stop conditioned air from escaping before it reaches the living space.
- [Airflow Testing](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/airflow-testing): Airflow Testing, called Ductwork Airflow Assessment, is a diagnostic process that measures air movement volume and velocity through an HVAC system.
- [Noise Level Considerations](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/noise-level-considerations): Noise Level Considerations, called Sound Output or AC Sound Assessment, are the evaluation and management of sound produced by air conditioning equipment to keep decibel levels within acceptable ranges for occupied spaces, covering compressor vibration, indoor-to-outdoor unit proximity, frequency range of emitted sound, distance-dependent noise measurement and the placement decisions that follow from each reading.
- [Old AC Unit Removal](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/old-ac-unit-removal): Old AC unit removal, called old air conditioner removal, is the disconnection, extraction, and disposal of an existing air conditioning unit before a new system goes in.
- [System Startup and Commissioning](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/system-startup-and-commissioning): System Startup and Commissioning, called AC commissioning, is the structured verification process that confirms a newly installed or replaced air conditioning system operates to its design specifications.
- [Refrigerant Management Regulations](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/refrigerant-management-regulations): Refrigerant Management Regulations, called F-Gas Regulations, are a type of Environmental Protection Regulations that govern the purchase, handling, recovery, reclamation and disposal of refrigerants used in HVAC systems, covering services from technician certification requirements and leak rate thresholds to GWP limits, reporting protocols and penalty provisions for non-compliance.
- [Installation Safety Measures](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/installation-safety-measures): Installation safety measures, called Workplace Safety Procedures, are mandatory procedural controls applied during AC installation to protect workers and building occupants from electrical hazards, refrigerant exposure, falls and structural damage.
- [HVAC Safety Standards](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/hvac-safety-standards): HVAC Safety Standards, called Mechanical Safety Regulations, are codified rules specifying the safe design, installation, inspection, and operation of heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems.
- [Building Codes Compliance](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/building-codes-compliance): Building Codes Compliance, called regulatory adherence, is a type of Regulatory Compliance that governs how HVAC equipment is selected, installed, inspected and approved across residential and commercial properties, covering jurisdiction-specific code versions, mechanical permit requirements, load calculation documentation, equipment clearance specifications, inspection records and approval certifications.
- [Permit Pull](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/permit-pull): Permit Pull, called the Permitting Process, is a type of administrative process in which a homeowner or licensed contractor submits an application to a local government authority to obtain official authorization before beginning construction, installation, or replacement work on a heating and cooling system, including central air conditioning systems, ductless mini split systems, heat pumps and related mechanical equipment.
- [HVAC Installation Permits](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/hvac-installation-permits): HVAC installation permits.
- [California Building Energy Efficiency Standards](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/california-building-energy-efficiency-standards): California Building Energy Efficiency Standards, known as the California Energy Code, are the mandatory statewide regulations that set minimum energy performance requirements for residential and nonresidential buildings, covering HVAC equipment efficiency ratings, building envelope thermal performance, insulation R-values by climate zone, lighting standards and mechanical ventilation requirements.
- [CSLB License](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/cslb-license): A CSLB License, formally called a California Contractor License, is a state-issued credential granted by the Contractors State License Board that authorizes individuals and companies to legally perform construction and specialty trade work in California, including HVAC installation, general building, plumbing, electrical, and dozens of other classifications.
- [Manufacturer Warranty Registration](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/manufacturer-warranty-registration): Manufacturer Warranty Registration, called Product Warranty Registration, is a formal administrative process in which a homeowner or installing contractor records a new equipment purchase with the manufacturer.
- [Rebates and Incentives](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/rebates-and-incentives): Rebates and incentives, called energy efficiency incentives or discounts, are financial reductions and credits offered by utility companies, equipment manufacturers, and government agencies to lower the net cost of qualifying HVAC installations, including central air conditioning systems, ductless mini split systems and heat pumps.
- [Utility Rebate Programs](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/utility-rebate-programs): Utility Rebate Programs, called Energy Rebates, are utility-funded cash-back programs that reward residential and commercial customers who install qualifying high-efficiency HVAC equipment, including central air conditioning systems, ductless mini split systems, heat pumps and other energy-efficient cooling and heating units.
- [Professional Installation Process](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/professional-installation-process): The professional installation process, called a certified installation workflow, is a defined sequence of technical steps executed by licensed HVAC technicians to site-assess, mount, connect, and commission an air conditioning system so it operates at full capacity from day one.
- [HERS Rating](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/hers-rating): HERS Rating.
- [HERS Verification Test](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/hers-verification-test): The HERS Verification Test.
- [Cost Estimation](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/cost-estimation): Cost estimation, called a Service Estimate or Installation Quote, is a structured calculation of projected expenses completed before AC installation work begins, covering labor costs, equipment pricing, site survey evaluation, material costs and overhead allocation so a homeowner knows the full financial scope before any work starts.
- [AHRI Certified Equipment](https://ac-plus-heating-air.mintlify.site/ahri-certified-equipment): AHRI Certified Equipment, known as AHRI verified equipment, is a type of HVAC Equipment Certification in which cooling and heating units are independently tested and verified by the Air-Conditioning, Heating, and Refrigeration Institute to confirm that published performance ratings match real-world output, covering rated capacity in BTU/hr, Seasonal Energy Efficiency Ratio (SEER2), Energy Efficiency Ratio (EER2), Heating Seasonal Performance Factor (HSPF2) and other efficiency metrics across central air conditioning systems, ductless mini split systems, heat pumps and packaged units.
